raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Prefill buckets match a request on its input length. In agentic workloads most of a long context is usually cached: a 130k-token turn may need only a few hundred new tokens of prefill, yet it lands in the long-prompt bucket, while cache-aware candidates ignore bucket ranges altogether.

## Modifications

`--route-by-uncached-tokens` (with `--policy cache_aware` and `--bucket-config`), off by default:

1. Warm requests: match prefill buckets on E, the input beyond the longest prefix any prefill worker can reuse according to the KV indexer. The request uses the buckets that hold E, and cache candidates outside them are dropped.
2. Cold requests (nothing reusable, or no answer from the indexer) are not matched to a bucket: the existing load-based selection picks among all prefill workers. This avoids stalling the warmup of an agentic benchmark, where every session's first turn is a long uncached prompt: matched on input length, all of them would queue on the long-prompt bucket while the other workers sit idle.
3. Idle spill: when every DP rank of every worker in E's buckets has pending prefill work, send a warm request to another worker with an idle DP rank. A rank's pending work is its queued requests plus the uncached tokens it still has to prefill, so a rank chunking a long prompt (empty queue) is not idle.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

DeepSeek-V4-Pro (FP4), MI355X, agentic coding traces, 192 concurrent sessions, 1 prefill node + 1 decode node (TP8/DP8 attention), shared UMBP host pool, same code and nodes for both rows:

| Prefill node | tok/s/GPU | TTFT p50 / p90 / p95 (s) | P90 interactivity |
|---|---|---|---|
| one TP8/EP8 DP-attention worker | 47,646 | 4.17 / 12.02 / 18.46 | 74.7 |
| TP4 worker (E > 8192) + DP4-attention worker (E ≤ 8192), this PR | 50,778 | 3.80 / 9.89 / 15.02 | 71.4 |

Interactivity is lower for two reasons. With faster prefill, more sessions are decoding at once (decode step time +1.8%), which accounts for about 40% of the gap. Both runs also use `--pd-stream-after-prefill` (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/45102), which counts decode output produced before the prefill request completes in TTFT instead of ITL; requests prefilled on the less loaded TP4 worker reach the client sooner, so less decode time lands in TTFT (0.69 s vs. 0.87 s per request on average), which accounts for about 55%.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Provide speed benchmark results.

nodes.body:
Pushed aef1e269509 on top of 570df9f to close two flag-on gaps I found while re-checking the fix:

1. **Cold requests skipped the bucket context caps.** `(None, None) if cold` built a bare `global_prefill` over every worker, so a 20k cold prompt could land on a bucket with `max_context_tokens: 10000` (and the same path fires for every request while the KV indexer is unavailable, since those outcomes map to `Empty`). Cold now draws from the union of buckets returned by `prefill_domains_for_any_extend`, so the spread you want is kept while `max_context_tokens` and the TTFT policy still apply.
2. **A warm request could get no worker.** With `short{max_extend 8192, max_context 10000}` and `long{min_extend 8193}`, a 20k prompt with 15/20 blocks on `long` has E = 5000: `short` rejects the context, `long` excludes E, and `select_prefill_worker` returned `ProposalEmpty` where flag-off serves it on `long`. When no bucket admits E, selection now falls back to input-length matching (and the cache winner is not filtered by an empty extend set).

Both arms are reachable only with `--route-by-uncached-tokens`, so flag-off routing is byte-for-byte unchanged. Added the two cases to `routes_prefill_buckets_by_uncached_tokens`; fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, and the 1094 lib tests are green locally. Feel free to reshape it if you prefer a different fallback.
The idle set never checks the target bucket's own limits.

For n>1 `request_input_tokens` is prompt length * n (preparation.rs:512) while `request_sequence_tokens` is the prompt length, so this estimate is n times too big and E saturates to 0 once the match ratio reaches 1/n. Should be `request_sequence_tokens`.

Nothing enforces the `--policy cache_aware` in the help text. With session_aware every request without a reusable prefix is cold and goes to the global domain, so bucket partitioning is silently off for that policy; with power_of_two the flag is dropped. Add it to the `tuned_cache_candidates` ensure.

nodes.body: Skipping `cache_winner` leaves `cache_gate_audit` at `None`, so a spill books `cache_aware_decisions_total{cache_miss}` even though the indexer had a hit. Needs its own label, or at least not cache_miss.

Fixed in 570df9f. The spill now draws its candidates from the prefill buckets whose context limit admits the request, ignoring only the extend range, and keeps each candidate in its own bucket domain, so that bucket's pending-prefill cap still applies.
Fixed: the estimate now uses `request_sequence_tokens`. The test now routes with n = 2 and includes a case where the old estimate drove E to 0.
Added it to the `tuned_cache_candidates` ensure, so any other policy is rejected at startup.

nodes.body: Spills now book `cache_aware_decisions_total{decision="idle_spill"}`, documented with the other labels, instead of falling through to `cache_miss`. I kept it separate from `cache_worker_queued`: a spill doesn't go through the queue gate and has no `diverted_overlap_blocks` sample.
